name: Anova Conventions
description: This module defines the naming, formatting, and structural style conventions to follow whenever writing, implementing, or reviewing anova code or output, so results stay consistent with the existing anova style guide.
content:
This module defines the naming, formatting, and structural style conventions to follow whenever writing, implementing, or reviewing anova code or output, so results stay consistent with the existing anova style guide.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Measure before optimizing any anova bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
2. Prefer the simplest anova approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
3. When multiple anova strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
4. Document any non-obvious anova decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
5. When anova guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
6. Surface known limitations of a chosen anova approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
7. Re-check edge cases relevant to anova (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
8. Prefer explicit, readable anova solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
9. Keep anova changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
10. Validate anova outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
11. Before starting anova work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
12. State assumptions about anova explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not silently drop anova edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Avoid introducing new anova abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of anova correctness.
- Do not apply generic anova advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Do not skip documenting anova assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for anova, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
